❗️🌀🇹🇼 - Super Typhoon Ragasa Devastates Taiwan, Threatens Region 

Super Typhoon Ragasa, the strongest tropical storm of 2025, struck eastern Taiwan, claiming at least 14 lives and leaving over 100 people missing. 

The typhoon prompted widespread evacuations in the Philippines and now endangers southern China, Hong Kong, Macau, and northern Vietnam.
  
Severe crosswinds from Ragasa forced Mandarin Airlines Flight AE1265, an ATR 72-600 from Taipei, to abort its initial landing attempt at Kinmen Airport. After a tense go-around, the flight landed safely on its second try, as captured in footage from TVBS.

Taiwanese authorities report that rescue operations are ongoing, with over 500 injuries recorded and significant damage to infrastructure. 

The storm’s impact has disrupted power for thousands and caused widespread flooding in eastern Taiwan, according to recent updates from Reuters.

🌀 Super Typhoon Ragasa Update 🌀

Good morning everyone,

The power of nature is on full display once again, this time across Taiwan, the Philippines, and now southern China, as Typhoon Ragasa*continues its destructive path.

In eastern Taiwan’s Guangfu, Hualien County, torrential rains and flooding have already left tragic consequences reports confirm fatalities, with at least 30 people missing after a lake overflowed, breaking a bridge and inundating the town with fast-moving floodwaters. Rescue teams are working tirelessly, but the scale of the damage is still being uncovered.

Ragasa, which just yesterday was a Super Typhoon at Category 5 strength, has weakened slightly, but don’t be fooled — with sustained winds of 140 mph (222 km/h, this storm is still the equivalent of a Category 4 hurricane, packing enough force to tear roofs off, flood cities, and topple power lines.

🌏 What’s Next?
The storm is now heading towards southern China, where tens of millions of people are on high alert. Ragasa is expected to skirt south of major urban giants like Hong Kong, Macau, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou, before slamming into Guangdong Province.

Authorities in China have activated full-scale emergency responses. Entire megacities are grinding to a halt:

 🚸 Schools are closed
 Businesses and offices shut down
 🚇 Public transport suspended
 🚐 Mass evacuations underway

In Shenzhen, officials are preparing to relocate 400,000 people from coastal and low-lying areas. Meanwhile, in Guangzhou (home to 18.6 million people), red alerts are expected to be raised to the highest warning possible.

The Hong Kong Observatory has warned of “phenomenal” ocean swells, with storm surges of up to 4 metres expected in some coastal areas by Wednesday. That’s enough to flood low-lying towns, swamp ports, and cause widespread destruction.

🏪 On the ground, supermarket shelves have been stripped bare as people rush to stockpile essentials. Videos already show chaotic scenes in Hong Kong, Zhuhai, and Shenzhen, as residents brace for what could be one of the most disruptive typhoons in recent memory.

A Season of Storms
Ragasa is the latest in a string of powerful typhoons this year, reminding us just how volatile the Western Pacific can be. Warm sea surface temperatures (fuelled by the lingering effects of El Niño earlier this year) have supercharged storm development, creating ideal conditions for these monsters of the sea.

The Philippines, already lashed by Ragasa, continues its recovery battered by destructive winds, landslides, and flooding. Now, southern China prepares for its turn.

Did you know?
Typhoons in this region are historically among the most damaging on Earth. Typhoon Mangkhut (2018) caused widespread devastation in almost the exact same areas Ragasa is now threatening, while Typhoon Hato (2017) cost Macau billions in damages. Ragasa could very well enter the same record books if the forecasts hold true.

Stay tuned for more updates later today including the latest model runs on Ragasa’s track and strength.

For now, let’s keep those affected in our thoughts. It’s a powerful reminder that while Cornwall may be enjoying calm skies under high pressure this week, elsewhere, the atmosphere is showing its raw and unforgiving power. 🌍

Kind regards,
KWT Dave
